issues.description: Step 1 calls DataFrame.append at line 17; pandas 3.0.6 no longer provides it. A one-line pd.concat replacement with ignore_index=False preserves the original append index and column-union behavior as a supported working-copy edit proposal.

Step 1 writes merged_raw_original.csv under its Fracfocus_raw working directory, while Step 2 changes to the FracFocusCSV parent and reads the same basename there. The producer/consumer paths must be aligned.

The Python stages and Stata do-file contain hard-coded Windows paths. This host uses a Linux workspace and the common README specifies host-wrapper paths must be relative or under [redacted-path-42901eaa63c4]; no author code was run.

Step 7 writes fracfocus_within_op.csv, fracfocus_between_op.csv and inn_validation.csv in the project root, while the do-file imports them from final_data; Step 6's well-level output is likewise written in the project root but imported from final_data.

The supplied Step 3 reads Austin Chalk for a kNN example and actively creates noise/cluster outputs only for Granite Wash, then comments to repeat the process for all shale samples. Step 4 globs those per-play outputs and the appendix lists play-specific parameters, so the full-play producer is missing.

Step 6 actively builds only 2012monthlevel.csv, then reads 2013monthlevel.csv through 2021monthlevel.csv. Its comment to repeat for all years is not an active producer; 2020–2021's documented averaging rule also needs to be encoded or supplied as prepared panels.

The datasheet and source comments explicitly provide manual QGIS producers for the urban, river/well/Shale Network monitor and PRISM grid exports, including the named outputs and stated join/radius settings. Remaining uncertainty concerns exact source layers, QGIS availability/version, coordinate systems, keys, output columns and row/cardinality contracts; the completed exports are not in the package. A single PATH lookup did not find the qgis executable; GUI/other-path availability is unverified, so this is a setup/configuration task, not a global access barrier.

Step 4's QGIS comment says 2019 TIGER/Line and MMSA polygons, while the output is converted to an urban flag using nonmissing NAME. The intended 2019 Urban Areas versus metropolitan/micropolitan layer must be confirmed before creating urban_joined.csv.

The Stata file imports final_data/refined_distance.csv and its comments specify the manual one-neighbor QGIS producer. The completed table is absent; exact source geometry, keys, distance units and consumed fields remain unresolved.

The current FracFocus download terms say its data may not be altered, while the author workflow cleans and transforms the disclosures. The terms applicable to the historical author export and the intended transformations need confirmation; this is not a conclusion about legal permissibility.

The author package contains source code, documentation and an identifier list, but no full analysis datasets or required prepared CSVs. Several mandatory files have no documented active producer or exact author route, so full dependency closure is incomplete.

COMP.FUNDA is a readable local candidate with the financial measures and fyear/tic fields, but the annual fiscal-year-to-well-calendar-year convention and ticker linkage used to build financial.csv are not specified.

Step 2 also uses legacy read_csv(squeeze=True) and tuple-based groupby column selections. Their compatibility with the installed pandas 3.0.6 and a semantics-preserving source change or author-supported compatible release remain unverified; no parser or code trial was run.

Well data: The chemical disclosure data are downloaded from FracFocus (access date: 21

evidence.description: Datasheet describes the WellDatabase match by API well number and the added play and first-six-month production fields.
evidence.quote:
Chemical identity is recorded as the CAS number in the FracFocus dataset. I strip all symbols
from the CAS numbers and manually check each CAS number in the CAS registry to make
sure that the chemicals are correctly reported.

I merge the well-level data with a commercial database, WellDatabase, which provides
additional well information (e.g., oil play and the first six-month oil and gas production data)
(access date: 20 January 2022). I use the API number to match the two datasets.

evidence.description: Datasheet defines the full chemical input and the minimum well/CAS/volume fields for the weighted Jaccard calculation.
evidence.quote:
I use the full chemical dataset (after cleaning the CAS number but before dropping any
observations) to construct the innovator measure. The detailed steps of constructing this
measure can be found in Section 5 and Appendix B. Since the chemical choices are compared
within each oil play, I split and save the chemical data by oil plays. I sort all wells based on
the reporting time and use the DBSCAN algorithm to identify novel formulas. The input of
the algorithm is a weighted Jaccard distance matrix, which contains the chemical choice
distance between each pair of wells. The minimum required information to compute the
concentrated-weighted Jaccard similarity includes the fracking job identifier, the CAS
number, and the injected volume of each chemical. I compare the chemical choice of each
newly drilled well with the prior 1,000 wells and check whether it is labeled as a noise (i.e.,
novel chemical choice) by the DBSCAN algorithm (the first 1,000 wells are solely used for

evidence.description: Datasheet specifies Water Quality Portal site/activity coverage in 2008–2021 and Shale Network data in 2011–2021.
evidence.quote:
Water monitor data: I obtain the water monitoring station data from the Water Quality Portal
(access date: 12 February 2022). The data can be downloaded from
https://www.waterqualitydata.us). I retrieve the site data and sampling activities between
2008 and 2021. The site data provides detailed information including the type of monitoring
station (e.g., well, stream, river, reservoir, etc.) and the geographic coordinates of each
monitoring station. I also download non-regulatory monitoring data from the Shale Network
website (access date: 12 January 2023). The data can be downloaded from
https://data.cuahsi.org. I retrieve the monitoring data from Shale Network between 2011 and
2021.

evidence.description: Datasheet specifies the PRISM grid variables and period, plus the same-month prior-three-year average for 2020–2021.
evidence.quote:
Seasonality data: I obtain fine-gridded PRISM weather data from Walfram Schlenker’s
website to construct the seasonality measure. The data can be downloaded from
http://www.columbia.edu/~ws2162/links.html. This data set covers daily minimum and
maximum temperature and total precipitation on a 2.5 x 2.5-mile grid for the contiguous
United States from 1950-2019. For 2020 and 2021, I use the average weather data for the
same month in the previous three years.

evidence.description: Online appendix identifies annual Compustat financial data and Factiva annual media coverage.
evidence.quote:
at the operator-year level. INNOVATIVE OP equals one if an operator is innovative in any
of its shale plays. I obtain firm-level annual financial data from Compustat and construct a
list of commonly used financial variables. I also include two additional variables to capture
the level of public scrutiny for each operator. TORT equals one if the operator has been
sued in tort during the sample period. LOG MEDIA is the annual media coverage of the
operator (log-transformed, obtained from Factiva), which proxies for media awareness. I find
that being innovative is associated with operator size, capital expenditure, and profitability.
